proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a row \(n\) and a law in \(\mathcal P\). By \(\texttt{ass:cell-mass}\) and \(\texttt{ass:instrument-overlap}\), for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
P_n(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)
=p_{n,x}e_{n,x}^{z}(1-e_{n,x})^{1-z}
\ge p_0\varepsilon .
\]
The row observations are independent by \(\texttt{ass:iid-row}\). Hence
\[
P_n(N_{n,x,z}=0)
=\{1-P_n(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)\}^{n}
\le (1-p_0\varepsilon)^n .
\]
The union bound over the \(2J\) pairs \((x,z)\) yields, uniformly in the law,
\[
P_n(\mathcal E_n^c)
\le\sum_{x=1}^J\sum_{z=0}^1P_n(N_{n,x,z}=0)
\le2J(1-p_0\varepsilon)^n\longrightarrow0.
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), \(N_{n,x,z}\ge1\) for both \(z\), hence \(N_{n,x}\ge2\), and
\[
\max\{N_{n,x},1\}=N_{n,x},\qquad
\max\{N_{n,x,z},1\}=N_{n,x,z},\qquad
\max\{N_{n,x,z}/n,1/n\}=N_{n,x,z}/n.
\]
Thus every totalized empirical proportion and every component of \(\widehat\psi_{w,n}\) equals its ordinary nonempty-cell formula. All remaining objects in the proposition are deterministic measurable compositions of those quantities under \(\texttt{def:finite-sample-totalization}\), \(\texttt{def:unscreened-plugin}\), \(\texttt{def:face-envelope}\), and \(\texttt{def:confidence-interval}\), so they also agree on \(\mathcal E_n\).

If the totalized and ordinary procedures are coupled to agree on \(\mathcal E_n\), then for any coverage event \(A_n\),
\[
\left|P_n(A_n^{\mathrm{tot}})-P_n(A_n^{\mathrm{ord}})\right|
\le P_n(\mathcal E_n^c)
\le2J(1-p_0\varepsilon)^n.
\]
This proves the proposition.

Write \(d=2JK\), \(w=w_n\), \(\widehat w=\widehat w_n\), and \(\Delta=\widehat w-w\). The proof has three steps.

First, use finite-multinomial Taylor expansion. Define the proof-intermediate event
\[
\mathcal F_n=\left\{\min_{x,z}N_{n,x,z}/n\ge p_0\varepsilon/2\right\}.
\]
Each joint-cell frequency has mean at least \(p_0\varepsilon\) and variance at most \(1/(4n)\). Chebyshev's inequality and a union bound over the \(2J\) cells give \(P_n(\mathcal F_n^c)\le C/n\) uniformly. On \(\mathcal F_n\), each coordinate of \(\widehat w\) is a twice continuously differentiable ratio of finitely many empirical cell probabilities on a neighborhood whose denominators are bounded below by \(p_0\varepsilon/2\). The first derivative is exactly the displayed influence vector \(\psi_{w,n}\), and the second derivatives are bounded by a constant depending only on \(p_0,\varepsilon,J,K\). Each remaining empirical cell frequency also has variance at most \(1/(4n)\), so the same variance calculation makes their joint error \(O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Taylor's formula then gives
\[
\sqrt n\Delta
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})+R_n,\qquad
\sup_{(P_n)\in\mathcal P}P_n(\|R_n\|>\eta)\longrightarrow0
\]
for every \(\eta>0\), and \(\|\Delta\|=O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly. The exponentially negligible complement \(\mathcal E_n^c\) is harmless by \(\texttt{prop:finite-sample-totalization}\). This uses \(\texttt{ass:iid-row}\), \(\texttt{ass:cell-mass}\), and \(\texttt{ass:instrument-overlap}\), which are member properties of \(\texttt{def:model-class}\).

Second, use the finite piecewise-linear secant technique. For a fixed orthant mask and compatible survivor-minimum, lower-gap, lower-maximum, upper-cut, and upper-cap choices, the definitions of \(\Pi_+\), \(m\), \(b_L\), and \(b_U\) give
\[
M(u)=B_r'u,\qquad N_L(u)=A_r^{L\prime}u,\qquad N_U(u)=A_r^{U\prime}u.
\]
Thus, wherever \(M(u)>0\), the endpoint maps \(F_L(u)=N_L(u)/M(u)\) and \(F_U(u)=N_U(u)/M(u)\) have the explicit gradients
\[
\nabla F_L(u)=\frac{A_r^L-F_L(u)B_r}{M(u)},\qquad
\nabla\{-F_U(u)\}=-\frac{A_r^U-F_U(u)B_r}{M(u)}.
\]
These are precisely the finite min--cut gradients encoded by \(A_r^L,A_r^U,B_r\); no latent optimization problem is invoked.

By \(\texttt{ass:aggregate-mass}\), \(M(w)\ge m_0\). Since \(M\) is a sum of finitely many minima of positive-part linear forms, it is globally Lipschitz. On \(\|\Delta\|\le m_0/(2L_M)\), the segment \(w_s=w+s\Delta\), \(0\le s\le1\), satisfies \(M(w_s)\ge m_0/2\). This event has probability tending to one uniformly. The segment meets finitely many regions. Subdivide at their crossing times; on an interval in a common boundary choose either incident region, since the formulas agree along that interval. The fundamental theorem of calculus gives
\[
F_L(\widehat w)-F_L(w)=\int_0^1\nabla F_{L,r(s)}(w_s)'\Delta\,ds,
\]
\[
F_U(w)-F_U(\widehat w)=\int_0^1\nabla\{-F_{U,r(s)}\}(w_s)'\Delta\,ds.
\]
The quotient gradients are uniformly Lipschitz on \(M\ge m_0/2\). Hence, for a constant \(C\) depending only on the fixed coefficient family and \(m_0\),
\[
F_L(\widehat w)-F_L(w)
\le\max_{r\in\mathcal S_n}g^L_{n,r}{}'\Delta+C\|\Delta\|^2,
\]
\[
F_U(w)-F_U(\widehat w)
\le\max_{r\in\mathcal S_n}g^U_{n,r}{}'\Delta+C\|\Delta\|^2,
\]
where \(\mathcal S_n\) is the set of regions encountered by the segment. Integration produces a convex combination of encountered linear forms, bounded by their maximum, and \(\sqrt n\|\Delta\|^2=o_{P_n}(1)\) uniformly.

Third, localize the encountered regions. Represent each region by its finite signed affine slacks, rescaled without changing signs so each is one-Lipschitz. If the segment enters a region, every defining inequality violated at \(w\) has violation at most \(\|\Delta\|\), by comparing \(w\) with the entry point. This covers projection releases, zero gaps, survivor minima, lower zero-or-cut comparisons, upper-cut comparisons, and upper mass caps. Because \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\),
\[
\|\Delta\|=o_{P_n}(a_n)
\]
uniformly. The deterministic localization constants in \(\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)\) therefore ensure
\[
\mathcal S_n\subseteq\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)
\]
with probability tending to one uniformly. Every empirical-population slack difference is at most a fixed multiple of \(\|\Delta\|\). The inner tolerance \(a_n/4\), empirical tolerance \(a_n\), and the same event give
\[
\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)\subseteq\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}.
\]
Here \(\texttt{ass:tolerance-vanishes}\) localizes the faces and \(\texttt{ass:tolerance-dominates-noise}\) supplies the inclusions.

When \(M(\widehat w)>0\), the capacity formulas imply \(0\le N_L(\widehat w)\le N_U(\widehat w)\le M(\widehat w)\), so endpoint clipping is inactive. The complementary event is negligible because \(M(\widehat w)=M(w)+o_{P_n}(1)\) and \(M(w)\ge m_0\). Multiplying the secant inequalities by \(\sqrt n\), substituting the first-step expansion, and applying the inclusions proves
\[
\max\{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_{L,n}-\theta_{L,n}),
\sqrt n(\theta_{U,n}-\widehat\theta_{U,n})\}
\le\max_{r\in\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)}
\left\{g^L_{n,r}{}'n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni}),
g^U_{n,r}{}'n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})\right\}
+o_{P_n}(1),
\]
uniformly, together with the asserted retention inclusion.

Let
\[
Z_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni}),\qquad
T_n=\max\{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_{L,n}-\theta_{L,n}),
\sqrt n(\theta_{U,n}-\widehat\theta_{U,n})\}.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:finite-secant-envelope}\), on events whose probabilities tend to one uniformly,
\[
T_n\le S_n+o_{P_n}(1),\qquad
S_n=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)}
\{g^L_{n,r}{}'Z_n,g^U_{n,r}{}'Z_n\},
\]
and \(\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)\subseteq\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\).

We establish the finite-dimensional Gaussian and multiplier comparison. The influence coordinates are uniformly bounded under \(\texttt{ass:cell-mass}\) and \(\texttt{ass:instrument-overlap}\). Expanding the characteristic function gives, for fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^{2JK}\),
\[
E_{P_n}e^{it'Z_n}
=\left(1-\frac{t'\Sigma_{w,n}t}{2n}
+O(n^{-3/2}\|t\|^3)\right)^n
=e^{-t'\Sigma_{w,n}t/2}+o(1),
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal P\). Tightness follows from the uniform second-moment bound. Thus every subsequence has a further subsequence on which \(Z_n\) converges to the centered Gaussian vector with the corresponding limiting covariance.

The covariance band transfers from conditional to unconditional capacities. Let \(\gamma_n\) be the stacked conditional contrast vector, let \(\psi_{\gamma,n}\) be its influence vector under total-sample \(\sqrt n\) scaling, and let \(P_n^{\mathrm{diag}}\) be the block-diagonal matrix with block \(p_{n,x}I_{2K}\). The influence decomposition is
\[
\psi_{w,n}=P_n^{\mathrm{diag}}\psi_{\gamma,n}
+\bigl((\mathbf1\{X=x\}-p_{n,x})\gamma_{n,x}\bigr)_{x\in\mathcal X}.
\]
The first summand has conditional mean zero given \(X\), while the second is a function of \(X\), so their cross covariance is zero. Therefore, on nonredundant coordinates,
\[
\Sigma_{w,n}\succeq
P_n^{\mathrm{diag}}\Sigma_{c,n}P_n^{\mathrm{diag}}
\succeq p_0^2\underline\lambda I
\]
by \(\texttt{ass:raw-covariance-band}\) and \(\texttt{ass:cell-mass}\). Uniform boundedness supplies a finite upper eigenvalue bound.

Define
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{w,n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
\widehat\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})\widehat\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})'.
\]
The ratio Taylor expansion in \(\texttt{lem:finite-secant-envelope}\) also gives
\[
n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
\|\widehat\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})-\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})\|^2=o_{P_n}(1)
\]
uniformly. For the oracle influence vectors, every covariance entry is an average of row-wise independent bounded variables and has variance at most \(C/n\). Expanding
\(\widehat\psi\widehat\psi'-\psi\psi'\), applying Cauchy--Schwarz, and using these two facts yields
\[
\|\widehat\Sigma_{w,n}-\Sigma_{w,n}\|=o_{P_n}(1),\qquad
\max_{r\in\mathcal R_n^0(P_n),\,e\in\{L,U\}}
\|\widehat g^e_{n,r}-g^e_{n,r}\|=o_{P_n}(1)
\]
uniformly. Conditional on the data, \(G_n^*\) is exactly \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_{w,n})\). Since \(\mathcal R\) is finite, these convergences imply convergence of every finite Gaussian maximum used below.

Quantiles require a separate degeneracy check. For a population-active face \(r\), a zero endpoint gradient means \(A_r^e=\theta_{e,n}B_r\). The coefficient pairs form a fixed finite set. Either \(A_r^e\) is proportional to \(B_r\), making the ratio constant on that region, or
\[
\inf_{\vartheta\in[0,1]}\|A_r^e-\vartheta B_r\|>0.
\]
Taking the minimum over the finite nonproportional collection and using \(m_0\le M_n\le1\) shows that every population-active nonconstant face has gradient norm bounded away from zero. Its variance on the nonredundant observable space is then bounded away from zero by the covariance band. If either endpoint has an active nonconstant face, the inner maximum contains such a centered nondegenerate normal form. Its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile is positive because \(\alpha<1/2\). At a positive argument, a finite Gaussian maximum has no atom: the event that its maximum equals \(t>0\) is contained in a finite union of events that a nondegenerate Gaussian coordinate equals \(t\). The variance bounds and finiteness make this continuity uniform at the positive quantiles, irrespective of additional near-active constant branches whose gradients may be small. If neither endpoint has an active nonconstant face, each active piece is constant. Any reachable nonconstant piece would be in \(\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)\) and would itself supply the preceding nondegenerate form; if there is none, continuity across common boundaries forces all reachable constant pieces for a given endpoint to have the same constant value. Both endpoint errors are then exactly zero on the localization event, and the nonnegative critical value covers them.

Let \(q_n^0\) be the conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the multiplier maximum restricted to \(\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)\), with estimated gradients. Set inclusion gives pathwise
\[
c_{n,1-\alpha}\ge q_n^0.
\]
The subsequence Gaussian comparison, covariance consistency, and the constant-or-continuous dichotomy imply
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal P}
P_n(T_n\le c_{n,1-\alpha})\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Indeed, any violating sequence has a subsequence on which the finite inner family is constant and all covariances, endpoint values, masses, and gradients converge; the preceding Gaussian calculation gives limiting probability at least \(1-\alpha\), a contradiction. The secant remainder is absorbed by uniform continuity at a positive quantile; in the all-constant case the exact local equality applies. No deterministic padding is used.

The retained family is nonempty. Its Gaussian maximum dominates any one of its centered Gaussian forms; such a form has median zero when nondegenerate, while all forms equal zero if the conditional maximum is wholly degenerate. Since \(1-\alpha>1/2\), this proves \(c_{n,1-\alpha}\ge0\). Therefore \(T_n\le c_{n,1-\alpha}\) implies
\[
\widehat\theta_{L,n}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n\le\theta_{L,n},\qquad
\theta_{U,n}\le\widehat\theta_{U,n}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n.
\]
Clipping preserves these inequalities because \(0\le\theta_{L,n}\le\theta_{U,n}\le1\). On the same high-probability neighborhood, \(\widehat M_n>0\) and the interval is ordered, so the off-support fallback is inactive. The established \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{PT}}\) mapping in \(\texttt{def:imported-partialtransport-mapping}\) supplies the distinct identification equality \(\Theta_{I,n}=[\theta_{L,n},\theta_{U,n}]\). Thus the displayed event implies \(\Theta_{I,n}\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n\), proving uniform whole-set coverage for all ties and changing-support arrays in \(\mathcal P\).

Call a choice population active when all defining signed slacks vanish or have the population-valid strict sign, and inactive when at least one required slack has the wrong sign. Under \(\texttt{ass:oracle-separation}\), every inactive alternative is separated from zero by at least \(\delta_0\), whereas every tied active alternative has zero slack.

The multinomial expansion in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\) gives \(\|\widehat w_n-w_n\|=O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\). Every projection, gap, survivor-minimum, lower-cut, upper-cut, and mass-cap slack belongs to a fixed finite family of affine functions, so all empirical slack errors are \(O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\). By \(\texttt{ass:tolerance-dominates-noise}\) and \(\texttt{ass:tolerance-vanishes}\),
\[
\max_s|\widehat s_n-s_n|=o_{P_n}(a_n),\qquad a_n<\delta_0/2
\]
with probability tending to one. On this event every zero-slack active choice is retained, every unique active sign is selected, and every inactive choice remains farther than \(a_n\) from the relevant boundary, maximum, or minimum. Compatibility is imposed in both Cartesian constructions. Hence
\[
P_n\{\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}=\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{act}}(P_n)\}\longrightarrow1.
\]

On this equality event, empirical and oracle maxima have the same finite index set. Moreover,
\[
\max_{r\in\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{act}}(P_n),\,e\in\{L,U\}}
\|\widehat g^e_{n,r}-g^e_{n,r}\|=o_{P_n}(1),\qquad
\|\widehat\Sigma_{w,n}-\Sigma_{w,n}\|=o_{P_n}(1),
\]
by the quotient formulas, \(M_n\ge m_0\), and the covariance calculation in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\). Conditional on the data, both critical values are quantiles of maxima of the same fixed finite number of centered Gaussian forms, with coefficients and covariances differing by \(o_{P_n}(1)\).

If an oracle gradient is nonzero, the constant-or-nondegenerate argument in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\) makes the oracle \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile positive and continuous, so convergence of the finite Gaussian vectors implies convergence of generalized-inverse quantiles. If every oracle gradient vanishes, every active quotient piece is constant; on the recovered family the empirical gradients vanish exactly and both critical values equal zero. Therefore
\[
c_{n,1-\alpha}-c^{\mathrm{oracle}}_{n,1-\alpha}=o_{P_n}(1),
\]
which proves both assertions.

Under the premise, the active family contains one compatible region for each endpoint and one common survivor-minimum choice in every cell. Positivity of every cell survivor mass and separation of all projection choices keep the segment from \(w_n\) to \(\widehat w_n\) in that region with probability tending to one. Let the two signed gradients be \(g_n^L\) and \(g_n^U\). The ordinary differentiable quotient rule and first-stage expansion give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_{L,n}-\theta_{L,n})
=g_n^{L\prime}n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})+o_{P_n}(1),
\]
\[
\sqrt n(\theta_{U,n}-\widehat\theta_{U,n})
=g_n^{U\prime}n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})+o_{P_n}(1).
\]
By \(\texttt{thm:oracle-face-equivalence}\), the retained family equals these active choices with probability tending to one and its critical value differs by \(o_{P_n}(1)\) from
\[
q_{1-\alpha}\!\left(
\max\{g_n^{L\prime}G_n^*,g_n^{U\prime}G_n^*\}
\mid O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\right).
\]
This is the ordinary joint one-sided Gaussian delta-method critical value for the two signed endpoint errors. The expansions and critical-value equality show that the interval endpoints differ from those of that ordinary interval by \(o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\). Clipping at the known support boundaries is common to both constructions and preserves first-order equivalence.

theorem.statement:
There is a fully specified studentized retention rule requiring no analyst-chosen sequence \(a_n\). Represent every compatible face \(r\in\mathcal R\) by the finite explicit signed affine inequalities \(\lambda_{rj}(w)\ge0\) obtained from its orthant signs, gap sign, survivor-minimum comparison, lower zero-or-cut comparisons, upper-cut comparisons, and mass-cap comparison. Estimate the standard deviation of each nonconstant slack from \(\widehat\psi_{w,n}\), and let the retention threshold be the conditional \((1-\beta_n)\)-quantile of the maximum of their absolute studentized common-multiplier scores, where \(\beta_n=1/\log(n\vee e^2)\). Retain \(r\) exactly when none of its studentized empirical inequality violations exceeds this threshold. Define \(\mathrm{CI}^{\mathrm{ad}}_n\) by the formula in \(\texttt{def:confidence-interval}\), replacing \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) in the endpoint-gradient multiplier maximum by this adaptive retained family. Then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal P}
P_n\{\Theta_{I,n}\subseteq\mathrm{CI}^{\mathrm{ad}}_n\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Under \(\texttt{ass:oracle-separation}\), the adaptive retained family equals the oracle active family with probability tending to one and its endpoint critical value differs from the oracle face-envelope critical value by \(o_{P_n}(1)\).
theorem.proof_tex:
We make the construction explicit. Because \(\mathcal R\) is finite and all projection and branch formulas are linear once an orthant mask is fixed, there are fixed coefficient vectors \(d_{rj}\) such that \(\lambda_{rj}(w)=d_{rj}'w\), after harmless positive rescaling, and face \(r\) is compatible at \(w\) exactly when every \(\lambda_{rj}(w)\ge0\). These are coordinate signs, the two signs of each total-mass gap, and the pairwise affine comparisons defining the displayed maxima and minima. Their enumeration uses explicit cuts and mass caps and no latent linear program.

Let \(\mathcal D\) be the indices for which \(d_{rj}\) is nonzero on the nonredundant observable contrast space. For \((r,j)\in\mathcal D\), define
\[
\widehat s_{rj}^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
\{d_{rj}'\widehat\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})\}^2,\qquad
H_n^*=\max_{(r,j)\in\mathcal D}
\frac{|d_{rj}'G_n^*|}{\widehat s_{rj}}.
\]
If an empirical standard deviation is zero, interpret its ratio as zero when its numerator is zero and \(+\infty\) otherwise; constant zero inequalities are always retained. Put \(\beta_n=1/\log(n\vee e^2)\), let \(k_n^*\) be the generalized-inverse conditional \((1-\beta_n)\)-quantile of \(H_n^*\), and define
\[
\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ad}}
=\left\{r\in\mathcal R:
\frac{\sqrt n[-\lambda_{rj}(\widehat w_n)]_+}{\widehat s_{rj}}
\le k_n^*\ \text{for every nonconstant defining inequality }j\right\}.
\]
This is a measurable implementation of \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\). Its vanishing probability level is fixed by formula and is not an analyst-specified tolerance.

Call a slack nonconstant when its coefficient is nonzero on the nonredundant observable contrast space; algebraic identities on the redundant complement are imposed deterministically and need no studentization. The covariance calculation in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\) implies that every nonconstant \(d_{rj}\) has population standard deviation bounded above and away from zero uniformly over \(\mathcal P\). Uniform covariance consistency gives the same for \(\widehat s_{rj}\) with probability tending to one. Conditional on the data, every standardized nonconstant coordinate in \(H_n^*\) is standard normal and their number is a fixed finite integer \(L\). Let \(\Phi\) denote the standard-normal distribution function. Gaussian domination and the union bound give
\[
\Phi^{-1}(1-\beta_n/2)
\le k_n^*
\le\Phi^{-1}(1-\beta_n/(2L))
\]
with probability tending to one. Hence
\[
k_n^*\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
k_n^*=O_{P_n}(\sqrt{\log\log n}),\qquad
k_n^*/\sqrt n\longrightarrow0
\]
uniformly.

If a region is encountered on the segment from \(w_n\) to \(\widehat w_n\), the entry argument in \(\texttt{lem:finite-secant-envelope}\) gives
\[
\sqrt n[-\lambda_{rj}(w_n)]_+=O_{P_n}(1)
\]
for all its defining inequalities. Taylor expansion adds another \(O_{P_n}(1)\) studentized term at \(\widehat w_n\). Since \(k_n^*\to\infty\), a union bound over the fixed family shows that every segment-encountered face belongs to \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ad}}\) with probability tending to one uniformly. Repeating the finite secant proof with this family and using \(k_n^*/\sqrt n\to0\) gives the same endpoint majorization. The multiplier and constant-or-nondegenerate quantile proof in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\) yields
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal P}
P_n\{\Theta_{I,n}\subseteq\mathrm{CI}^{\mathrm{ad}}_n\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]

Under \(\texttt{ass:oracle-separation}\), an active zero slack has studentized empirical violation \(O_{P_n}(1)\) and is retained because \(k_n^*\to\infty\). An inactive choice has violation at least \(\delta_0+o_{P_n}(1)\), so its score is of order \(\sqrt n\), exceeding \(k_n^*=O_{P_n}(\sqrt{\log\log n})\). Thus \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ad}}\) equals the oracle family with probability tending to one. Conditional covariance and gradient consistency, followed by the generalized-inverse quantile argument in \(\texttt{thm:oracle-face-equivalence}\), gives an \(o_{P_n}(1)\) critical-value difference. This proves both properties without an analyst-specified sequence \(a_n\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(k\in\mathcal Y\).  All equalities between potential variables in the hypotheses are understood \(P_n\)-almost surely.  By \(\texttt{ass:cell-mass}\) and the declared condition \(p_0>0\),
\[
P_n(X_{n1}=x)=p_{n,x}\ge p_0>0.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:instrument-overlap}\), the definition of \(e_{n,x}\), and \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\),
\[
P_n(Z_{n1}=1\mid X_{n1}=x)=e_{n,x}\ge\varepsilon>0,
\qquad
P_n(Z_{n1}=0\mid X_{n1}=x)=1-e_{n,x}\ge\varepsilon>0.
\]
Thus every conditional probability below is defined on an event of positive probability.

Perfect compliance and treatment consistency give
\[
D_{n1}=D_{n1}(Z_{n1})=Z_{n1}.
\]
Universal selection and selection consistency then give
\[
S_{n1}=S_{n1}(D_{n1})=1.
\]
On this event, outcome consistency gives \(Y_{n1}=Y_{n1}(D_{n1})\).  Consequently, using first the definition of the observed selected-outcome cells and then conditional instrument exogeneity,
\[
\begin{aligned}
q^1_{n,1,x,k}
&=P_n(D_{n1}=1,S_{n1}=1,Y_{n1}=k\mid Z_{n1}=1,X_{n1}=x)\\
&=P_n(Y_{n1}(1)=k\mid Z_{n1}=1,X_{n1}=x)\\
&=P_n(Y_{n1}(1)=k\mid X_{n1}=x)
=f_{1,n,x,k},\\
q^1_{n,0,x,k}&=0,\\
q^0_{n,0,x,k}
&=P_n(D_{n1}=0,S_{n1}=1,Y_{n1}=k\mid Z_{n1}=0,X_{n1}=x)\\
&=P_n(Y_{n1}(0)=k\mid Z_{n1}=0,X_{n1}=x)\\
&=P_n(Y_{n1}(0)=k\mid X_{n1}=x)
=f_{0,n,x,k},\\
q^0_{n,1,x,k}&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The two zero equalities follow because the conditioning event fixes \(D_{n1}=Z_{n1}\).  The definitions of the raw capacities therefore yield
\[
\ell_{n,x,k}=q^1_{n,1,x,k}-q^1_{n,0,x,k}=f_{1,n,x,k},
\qquad
h_{n,x,k}=q^0_{n,0,x,k}-q^0_{n,1,x,k}=f_{0,n,x,k}.
\]

Put
\[
\varphi_{n,x}
=\bigl(f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},
f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1}\bigr)^{\prime}.
\]
The definition of the unconditional raw-capacity block now gives
\[
w_{n,x}=p_{n,x}\varphi_{n,x}.
\]
Every coordinate of \(\varphi_{n,x}\) is nonnegative, so the coordinatewise definition of \(\Pi_+\) implies
\[
(\Pi_+w_n)_x=w_{n,x}=p_{n,x}\varphi_{n,x}.
\]
Because each conditional potential-outcome marginal is a probability mass function,
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}f_{1,n,x,k}
=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}f_{0,n,x,k}=1.
\]
Hence, by the definition of \(m\),
\[
m((\Pi_+w_n)_x)
=\min\left\{p_{n,x}\sum_k f_{1,n,x,k},
p_{n,x}\sum_k f_{0,n,x,k}\right\}=p_{n,x}.
\]
Summing over the finite support and using \(\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_{n,x}=1\) proves
\[
M_n=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}m((\Pi_+w_n)_x)=1.
\]

We next use elementary positive homogeneity of the corrected finite cut formulas.  For every \(c\ge0\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_+^{2K}\), multiplication of every affine branch by \(c\), together with
\(\min\{ca,0\}=c\min\{a,0\}\), gives
\[
b_L(cv)=c,b_L(v),
\qquad
b_U(cv)=c,b_U(v).
\]
This is a direct max--min calculation from the corrected definitions of \(b_L\) and \(b_U\); no optimization problem is latent in the step.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
N_{L,n}
&=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}b_L((\Pi_+w_n)_x)
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_{n,x}b_L(\varphi_{n,x}),\\
N_{U,n}
&=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}b_U((\Pi_+w_n)_x)
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_{n,x}b_U(\varphi_{n,x}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitution of these identities and \(M_n=1\) into \(\texttt{def:sharp-benefit-set}\), whose sharpness and endpoint attainability are supplied by \(\texttt{def:imported-partialtransport-mapping}\), yields exactly
\[
\Theta_{I,n}
=\left[
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_{n,x}b_L(\varphi_{n,x}),
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_{n,x}b_U(\varphi_{n,x})
\right].
\]
Moreover, perfect compliance implies \(C_{n1}=1\), and universal selection implies \(A_{n1}=1\).  Thus the causal target reduces to
\[
\theta_n=P_n\{Y_{n1}(1)>Y_{n1}(0)\},
\]
whereas the displayed interval is an observed-marginal sharp identifying functional; their relationship is the sharpness conclusion imported above, not a definition of \(\theta_n\).

It remains to verify the named ordinary-bound reduction.  Suppress \(x\), write
\(r_k=f_{1,n,k}\), \(s_k=f_{0,n,k}\), and define
\[
\Delta_j=\sum_{k=j}^{K-1}(r_k-s_k),
\qquad 0\le j\le K,
\]
so \(\Delta_0=\Delta_K=0\).  Equal total masses make the gap term in the corrected lower formula zero, and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_L((r,s))
&=\max\left\{0,\max_{0\le t<K}\sum_{k\le t}(s_k-r_k)\right\}\\
&=\max\left\{0,\max_{0\le t<K}\Delta_{t+1}\right\}
=\max_{0\le j<K}\Delta_j.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the upper formula, for every \(0\le j<K\),
\[
\sum_{k<j}s_k+\sum_{k>j}r_k
=1+\Delta_j-r_j.
\]
The cut with \(j=0\) is at most one, so the outer mass cap is redundant, and
\[
b_U((r,s))
=1+\min_{0\le j<K}(\Delta_j-r_j).
\]
These are precisely the sharp strict-benefit formulas in \(\texttt{lem:lu-ding-dasgupta-strict-benefit-bounds}\), with their category count renamed from \(J\) to \(K\).  This proves the unstratified Lu--Ding--Dasgupta reduction.  Applying the same finite formulas conditionally in each positive-mass covariate cell and averaging with \(p_{n,x}\), as already derived above, proves the stated covariate-stratified reduction.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(r=(r_0,\ldots,r_{K-1})\) and \(s=(s_0,\ldots,s_{K-1})\) be probability vectors on \(\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), and put \(\Delta_j=\sum_{k=j}^{K-1}(r_k-s_k)\). Among all couplings \((U,V)\) with respective marginals \(r\) and \(s\), the sharp lower and upper bounds on \(P(U>V)\) are \(\max_{0\le j<K}\Delta_j\) and \(1+\min_{0\le j<K}(\Delta_j-r_j)\), respectively.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(b_L(v)\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen formula has the treatment and control capacity blocks reversed and therefore bounds strict harm, not strict benefit. As an explicit certificate, with \(v^{\ell}\) concentrated at \(K-1\) and \(v^h\) concentrated at \(0\), the frozen formula returns zero although every coupling has benefit probability one. Swapping the two blocks gives the strict-benefit lower capacity and matches Lu--Ding--Dasgupta Proposition 2 when both totals equal one.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(b_U(v)\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen upper-cut formula is oriented toward \(Y(0)>Y(1)\). Swapping the treated and control blocks yields the finite min-cut upper capacity for \(Y(1)>Y(0)\), and is required for coherence with the declared target estimand.

proposed.name: \(A^L_r\)
proposed.def: For each cell, let \(D\) be the diagonal zero-one mask recorded by \(r\). The zero branch contributes \(0\); a cut \(t\) with gap branch \(\gamma\in\{0,1\}\) contributes \(D[(-\mathbf 1\{k\le t\}+\gamma\mathbf 1_K)_{k=0}^{K-1},(\mathbf 1\{k\le t\}-\gamma\mathbf 1_K)_{k=0}^{K-1}]^{\prime}\). Stack these cell vectors over \(x\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This coefficient must be the branch gradient of the corrected \(b_L\). The corrected cut is \(\sum_{k\le t}(v^h_k-v^{\ell}_k)+\gamma(\sum_kv^{\ell}_k-\sum_kv^h_k)\), whose two coefficient blocks are the proposed ones.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(A^U_r\)

proposed.name: \(A^U_r\)
proposed.def: For each cell mask \(D\), an upper cut \(t\) contributes \(D[(\mathbf 1\{k>t\})_{k=0}^{K-1},(\mathbf 1\{k<t\})_{k=0}^{K-1}]^{\prime}\); a mass-cap branch contributes either \(D[(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime},0^{\prime}]^{\prime}\) or \(D[0^{\prime},(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime}]^{\prime}\) according to the selected survivor minimum. Stack over \(x\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This coefficient must be the branch gradient of the corrected upper cut \(\sum_{k<t}v^h_k+\sum_{k>t}v^{\ell}_k\). The mass-cap coefficients are unchanged.

proposed.statement: Under perfect compliance, \(D_{ni}(0)=0\) and \(D_{ni}(1)=1\), and universal selection, \(S_{ni}(0)=S_{ni}(1)=1\), one has \(\ell_{n,x,k}=f_{1,n,x,k}\), \(h_{n,x,k}=f_{0,n,x,k}\), \(w_{n,x}=p_{n,x}(f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}\), and \(M_n=1\). Consequently \(\Theta_{I,n}=[\sum_x p_{n,x}b_L((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}),\sum_x p_{n,x}b_U((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime})]\), the covariate-stratified ordinary sharp ordinal-benefit bounds; without covariate stratification these are the Lu--Ding--Dasgupta bounds.
proposed.justification: This reduction checks that the selected-complier capacity formulas collapse to the established ordinal-benefit geometry when compliance and observability cease to be latent.
proposed.gap: Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta establish the ordinary ordinal-benefit bounds; this proposition is a required reduction, not a novelty claim.
proposed.consumer: It gives implementers an exact benchmark for validating the capacity and min-cut code against standard two-arm ordinal data.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses the frozen conditional-IV exogeneity, consistency, cell-mass, and instrument-overlap assumptions, and the named Lu--Ding--Dasgupta result. These load-bearing dependencies were missing from the target metadata; the claim text itself is unchanged.

proofs.proof_tex:
\emph{Technique.}  We use direct finite-atom enumeration for the probability and identification calculations, the quotient-rule influence function for conditional multinomial probabilities for the covariance calculation, and an explicit rank-two spectral decomposition for the eigenvalue calculation.

Write \(m_x=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}\).  Because \(n\geq 16\),
\[
0<m_2=n^{-1/2}\leq \frac14,
\qquad
m_1=\frac14.
\]
Consequently all four displayed atom weights in \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) are nonnegative.  For each fixed \((x,z,r)\), their sum is
\[
\frac1{48}+\frac1{48}+\frac{m_x}{12}
 +\frac{1/2-m_x}{12}
=\frac1{24}+\frac1{24}=\frac1{12}.
\]
There are three values of \(r\), so \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)=1/4\) for each \((x,z)\); summing over the four pairs proves that the table has total mass one.  It also gives
\[
p_{n,x}=\sum_{z=0}^1\frac14=\frac12,
\qquad
e_{n,x}=\frac{P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=1)}{p_{n,x}}
=\frac{1/4}{1/2}=\frac12,
\]
where the division is valid because \(p_{n,x}=1/2>0\).

Conditional on \((X_{n1},Z_{n1})=(x,z)\), the four rows for a fixed \(r\) have probabilities
\[
\frac1{12},\quad \frac1{12},\quad
\frac{m_x}{3},\quad \frac{1/2-m_x}{3},
\]
respectively.  This conditional distribution of
\((D_{n1}(0),D_{n1}(1),S_{n1}(0),S_{n1}(1),Y_{n1}(0),Y_{n1}(1))\)
does not depend on \(z\), which verifies \(\texttt{ass:instrument-exogeneity}\).  The construction in \(\texttt{def:witness-atom-law}\) generates the observed variables as
\(D_{ni}=D_{ni}(Z_{ni})\), \(S_{ni}=S_{ni}(D_{ni})\), and
\(Y_{ni}=Y_{ni}(D_{ni})\) when \(S_{ni}=1\); hence the three consistency assumptions hold.  The potential selection and outcomes in every atom are indexed only by treatment, so \(\texttt{ass:exclusion}\) holds.  The only treatment-type pairs are
\[
(D_{ni}(0),D_{ni}(1))\in\{(1,1),(0,0),(0,1)\},
\]
which proves \(D_{ni}(1)\geq D_{ni}(0)\) and thus \(\texttt{ass:no-defiers}\).  On both complier rows, \(S_{ni}(1)-S_{ni}(0)=0\).  With \(\sigma_{n,x}=1\), this proves the inequality in \(\texttt{ass:weak-selection-monotonicity}\).  Finally, take the observations in each row to be independent copies of this one-unit law, as specified by \(\texttt{ass:iid-row}\).

We next enumerate the observed selected cells.  At \(z=0\), only the always-taker row contributes to \((D,S,Y)=(1,1,k)\), whereas the never-taker and always-selected-complier rows contribute to \((D,S,Y)=(0,1,k)\).  At \(z=1\), the roles are reversed.  Dividing the relevant atom weights by \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)=1/4\) yields, for every \(x\in\{1,2\}\) and \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
q^1_{n,0,x,k}=\frac1{12},
\qquad
q^1_{n,1,x,k}=\frac1{12}+\frac{m_x}{3},
\]
\[
q^0_{n,1,x,k}=\frac1{12},
\qquad
q^0_{n,0,x,k}=\frac1{12}+\frac{m_x}{3}.
\]
The four atom types exhaust the support, so these are all the nonzero selected observed cells.  By the definitions of the raw capacities,
\[
\ell_{n,x,k}=q^1_{n,1,x,k}-q^1_{n,0,x,k}=\frac{m_x}{3},
\qquad
h_{n,x,k}=q^0_{n,0,x,k}-q^0_{n,1,x,k}=\frac{m_x}{3}.
\]

Let \(v_x=(\Pi_+w_n)_x\).  Since \(p_{n,x}=1/2\) and the preceding contrasts are nonnegative, projection leaves the block unchanged and
\[
v_x^\ell=v_x^h=\frac{m_x}{6}(1,1,1)^{\prime}.
\]
Thus \(\sum_kv_{x,k}^\ell=\sum_kv_{x,k}^h=m_x/2\), and the definition of \(m(\cdot)\) gives
\[
m(v_x)=\frac{m_x}{2}.
\]
For every \(t\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
\sum_{k\leq t}(v_{x,k}^\ell-v_{x,k}^h)=0,
\qquad
\min\!\left\{\sum_kv_{x,k}^h-\sum_kv_{x,k}^\ell,0\right\}=0.
\]
The explicit lower-capacity formula therefore gives \(b_L(v_x)=0\).  For the upper capacity, there are exactly two coordinates among the conditions \(k<t\) and \(k>t\), for each \(t\in\{0,1,2\}\).  Hence
\[
\sum_{k<t}v_{x,k}^\ell+\sum_{k>t}v_{x,k}^h
=2\frac{m_x}{6}=\frac{m_x}{3},
\]
and, since \(m_x/3\leq m_x/2\), the explicit upper-capacity formula gives \(b_U(v_x)=m_x/3\).

Summing the two cell contributions and substituting \(m_1=1/4\) and \(m_2=n^{-1/2}\) now gives
\[
M_n=\frac{m_1+m_2}{2}=\frac18+\frac1{2\sqrt n},
\qquad
N_{L,n}=0,
\qquad
N_{U,n}=\frac{m_1+m_2}{3}=\frac1{12}+\frac1{3\sqrt n}.
\]
In particular \(M_n>0\), so both endpoint divisions are valid, and
\[
\frac{N_{L,n}}{M_n}=0,
\qquad
\frac{N_{U,n}}{M_n}
=\frac{(m_1+m_2)/3}{(m_1+m_2)/2}=\frac23.
\]
The established exact partial-transport mapping in \(\texttt{def:imported-partialtransport-mapping}\) states that these observed-law functionals are the attained sharp endpoints, rather than defining the causal target to equal them.  It follows that
\[
\Theta_{I,n}=\left[\frac{N_{L,n}}{M_n},\frac{N_{U,n}}{M_n}\right]
=\left[0,\frac23\right].
\]
Under the particular displayed latent coupling, \(Y_{n1}(1)=Y_{n1}(0)\) on every atom.  Moreover,
\[
P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(C_{n1}=1,A_{n1}=1)
=\sum_{x=1}^2p_{n,x}m_x=M_n>0.
\]
Thus its causal target is well defined and equals \(\theta_n=0\), which belongs to the sharp observed-law set above.  Sharpness of the full interval, including attainability of its other points by compatible latent couplings, is supplied by the imported identification result rather than by this one diagonal witness coupling.

It remains to calculate the covariance.  Fix a covariate cell and abbreviate \(m=m_x\),
\[
A=A_m=\frac{1/4+m}{3},
\qquad B=\frac1{12},
\qquad c=A+B.
\]
At \(z=1\), the probabilities of the three selected treated categories are each \(A\), and those of the three selected control categories are each \(B\).  Give the treated indicators sign \(+1\) and the control indicators sign \(-1\).  The resulting signed one-hot vector has mean
\[
v_0=(A,A,A,-B,-B,-B)^{\prime}
\]
and second-moment matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(A,A,A,B,B,B)\).  At \(z=0\), give the treated indicators sign \(-1\) and the control indicators sign \(+1\).  Its mean and second-moment matrix are
\[
v_1=(-B,-B,-B,A,A,A)^{\prime},
\qquad
\operatorname{diag}(B,B,B,A,A,A),
\]
respectively.  The quotient rule for a conditional probability \(P(H\mid C)\) gives influence function
\[
\frac{\mathbf 1\{C\}}{P(C)}\{\mathbf 1\{H\}-P(H\mid C)\}.
\]
Here \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)=1/4\).  The two instrument-cell contributions have disjoint supports and conditional mean zero.  Therefore the covariance of the six conditional contrasts under total-sample \(\sqrt n\) scaling is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma_x
&=4\Bigl\{\operatorname{diag}(A,A,A,B,B,B)-v_0v_0^{\prime}\\
&\hspace{28mm}+\operatorname{diag}(B,B,B,A,A,A)-v_1v_1^{\prime}\Bigr\}\\
&=4\{cI_6-v_0v_0^{\prime}-v_1v_1^{\prime}\}
=\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m).
\end{aligned}
\]
For distinct covariate cells, the corresponding influence functions have disjoint supports and mean zero, so their cross-covariance is zero.  Hence \(\Sigma_{c,n}\) is block diagonal with blocks
\(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,1})\) and
\(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,2})\).

For completeness, we diagonalize each block explicitly.  Let
\[
u_\ell=3^{-1/2}(1,1,1,0,0,0)^{\prime},
\qquad
u_h=3^{-1/2}(0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\prime}.
\]
On the four-dimensional orthogonal complement of
\(\operatorname{span}\{u_\ell,u_h\}\), both \(v_0v_0^{\prime}\) and \(v_1v_1^{\prime}\) vanish, so the eigenvalue is
\[
4c=\frac{2+4m}{3}
\]
with multiplicity four.  In the orthonormal basis \((u_\ell,u_h)\), the matrix
\(v_0v_0^{\prime}+v_1v_1^{\prime}\) is
\[
3\begin{pmatrix}
A^2+B^2&-2AB\\
-2AB&A^2+B^2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its eigenvalues are \(3(A-B)^2\) and \(3(A+B)^2\).  Since
\(A-B=m/3\) and \(A+B=c=(1+2m)/6\), the remaining two eigenvalues of \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m)\) are
\[
4\{c-3(A-B)^2\}=\frac{2+4m-4m^2}{3}
\]
and
\[
4\{c-3(A+B)^2\}=\frac{1-4m^2}{3}.
\]
This proves the asserted spectrum and its multiplicities.

Both witness masses lie in \((0,1/4]\).  On \([0,1/4]\), the first displayed eigenvalue lies in \([2/3,1]\); the second is increasing and lies in \([2/3,11/12]\); and the third is decreasing and lies in \([1/4,1/3]\).  Thus every eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_{c,n}\) lies in \([1/4,1]\), and in particular the entire twelve-dimensional contrast space is nonredundant.

We finally check the numerical restrictions defining \(\mathcal P\).  The equalities \(p_{n,x}=e_{n,x}=1/2\) imply \(p_{n,x}\geq p_0\) when \(p_0\leq1/2\), and
\(\varepsilon\leq e_{n,x}\leq1-\varepsilon\) when \(\varepsilon\leq1/2\).  Also
\[
M_n=\frac18+\frac1{2\sqrt n}\geq\frac18\geq m_0
\]
when \(m_0\leq1/8\).  The spectral calculation verifies
\(\texttt{ass:raw-covariance-band}\) whenever
\(\underline\lambda\leq1/4\) and \(\overline\lambda\geq1\).  Together with the sampling, IV, consistency, exclusion, treatment-monotonicity, and selection-monotonicity checks above, these are every member property in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\).  Therefore \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\in\mathcal P\) under the constants stated in the proposition.
